SRT Performance Joins the 2026 SEMA Show Featuring the First-Ever Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept
15 photos
Photo: Jeep
The Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept, prepared for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, is the first model from specialty brand Jeep with an SRT badge – more could be on the horizon in the coming years.
Jeep has been pretty busy lately, as it strives to bring out enough novelties to snatch the leadership among Stellantis brands in America back from Ram Trucks. So, we have seen what’s new about the 2027 Compass, 2027 Gladiator, 2027 Wrangler, 2027 Cherokee, the new 35-inch Tire Launch Edition for the Gladiator, or the 2027 Switchback that completes the year-long Twelve 4 Twelve series for the Wrangler nameplate, as well as Jeep being named the official 4x4 of the city of Moab.
And that was all in October 2026 alone! Now, Stellantis is kicking off November for the Jeep brand with the reveal of the Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept, the first concept model from Jeep wearing the SRT badge as it reimagines the American off-road icon. This prototype obviously pays tribute as it reimagines the legendary Jeep CJ-8 Scrambler with a combination of “open-air freedom, pickup versatility, authentic Jeep capability and unmistakable SRT attitude.”
It was developed starting from a Jeep Wrangler SUV foundation, rather than the Gladiator pickup truck sibling, and the “concept channels the original Scrambler’s spirit of adventure and individuality” via new proportions, a rugged utility flair, and “an uncompromising SRT performance vision.” This is a high-speed desert runner, a true V8-powered off-road beast.
“The original Scrambler became an icon because it broke the rules. It looked different, worked differently, and represented a certain kind of freedom that resonated with enthusiasts then and still does today,” said Tim Kuniskis, head of American Brands, SRT Performance and Direct Connection division, Stellantis North America. The new version is a two-door pickup with a usable truck bed and completely throws the Wrangler rule book out the window by packing the first independent front suspension ever offered on a Wrangler.
The bespoke high-travel independent front suspension, developed with off-road racing champion Casey Currie, is mixed with a trophy-truck-inspired rear axle, a heavy-duty wheel package, and desert-racing-focused hardware. There are also longer doors than on a Wrangler, a bespoke rear, an integrated pickup bed, a tailgate, bespoke fender flares, and a structural roll cage, along with Punk’n orange paint, bronze beadlock wheels, and SRT touches.
Under the hood, the company strapped in the 6.4-liter Hemi V8, but the concept is mostly about future hardware rather than a preview of an upcoming production truck. Alas, it does come with an integrated pickup bed and custom rear-seat system to switch between cargo and passenger-carrying capabilities, and the rear seats clip directly into floor-mounted hooks and can be completely removed or faced toward the front or the rear.
Inside, the cockpit has performance-focused seats, Dark Graphite leather, orange inserts, contrast stitching, bronze accents, and SRT embroidery, as well as custom grab handles, trim treatments, and a rear-seat Jeep Multi-panel System. So, what do you think – yay or nay?
